about: Public-notice channels per operator or agency: pages, sites, feeds, lists and accounts through which the public is told of sewage discharges, by law, permit or voluntarily. Read by pipeline/ingest/notification_pages.py (schema and validator there; test tests/test_notice_channels.py).

channels.name: County health officers: beach closure hotlines
channels.legal_basis: Health and Safety Code 115885(a)(1)(D): the health officer shall "Establish a telephone hotline to inform the public of all beaches currently closed, posted, or otherwise restricted"; 115885(a)(1)(F) and 17 CCR 7958: on a known untreated sewage release, "Immediately post and close the beach or a portion thereof, or otherwise restrict its use until the source of the sewage release is eliminated"
channels.note: The public channel the law names for beach closures and postings, including those after a sewage release, is a telephone hotline in each coastal county: hotline only, with no duty to publish closures on the web. Several counties also post them on voluntary web pages (rows below). (research/ca/report.md §2.1)

channels.name: County health officers: beach closure and posting signs

channels.note: Signs posted at the beach when it is closed or restricted after a known sewage release, until the source is eliminated and sampling allows reopening (17 CCR 7958). (research/ca/report.md §2.1)

channels.agency: California State Water Resources Control Board
channels.name: California State Water Board (CIWQS sanitary sewer spill reports)
channels.legal_basis: Order WQ 2022-0103-DWQ Att. E1 3.1.1: "Within three (3) business days of the Enrollee's knowledge of a Category 1 spill, the Enrollee shall submit a Draft Spill Report to the online CIWQS Sanitary Sewer System Database"; 3.1.2: a Certified Spill Report "Within 15 calendar days of the spill end date"; 3.2 the same for Category 2 spills; 3.3 Category 3 spills certified monthly
channels.note: The Board's nightly file of every Category 1, 2 and 3 spill reported under the Statewide Sanitary Sewer Systems General Order since June 2023, with start, end once certified, a point, volumes and the receiving water; it covers every enrollee (public agencies, and private systems the Board requires to enroll). Drafts arrive within 3 business days of a spill (median 2 days from its start in 2026); the end and the receiving water come only with certification, within 15 days of the spill's end. Category 4 spills (under 50 gallons, no surface water) are reported as monthly counts only. (research/ca/report.md §2.2)
